rule: Source-first visual curation authorised by operator. Local notes and assessment sources may be inventoried as reference candidates; learner reuse needs explicit rights and semantic review. Never copy an examination question into a new activity. Web seeds were re-inspected on 2026-10-18; inspection findings sit in each record.

assets.title: Ranunculus root cross-section
assets.source_locator: Commons file summary, original file and licensing section; inspected 2026-10-18

rights.status: file-specific licence recorded; attribution review pending
rights.creator: Sadierath

suitability_concerns: 648 × 485 original; confirm tissue visibility before labelling.
Original already has answer labels. It is a teaching/reference view, not a neutral assessment stimulus; acquire a distinct unlabelled field for testing. Proposed stimulus mapping is not approved.
Inspected 2026-10-18: labels include terms beyond the syllabus (tracheids, amyloplasts, vessel element, pericycle); a teaching variant must relabel with syllabus terms (xylem, phloem).
Labels are burnt in, so a neutral question variant needs the labels covered; flag that cover patches are an edit to the image.

scale.note: SCALE BAR LABEL WRONG: the bar spans most of the stele but is labelled "3 µm"; a root stele is hundreds of µm across. Preserve the original, but never use this bar for size calculations; mask or relabel it only in a flagged teaching variant after review.

structures_missing: epidermis (field shows the central stele only)

assets.title: Alternative dicot root cross-section
assets.source_locator: Commons file summary, original file and licensing section; inspected 2026-10-18

rights.status: file-specific licence recorded; attribution review pending
rights.creator: Nbnidhi

suitability_concerns: Candidate variation; independent review must confirm correct species/tissues.
Low-detail field: identity and tissue visibility remain uncertain. Do not certify dicot anatomy from the file title alone.

Inspected 2026-10-18: TISSUE IDENTITY UNCERTAIN. The field is dominated by large round spaces, more like aerenchyma or a monocot or aquatic specimen than a typical dicot root; the eyepiece vignette and blur limit use. Do not use until a botanist confirms the organ.
Commons description reads only "Dicot"; it does not identify the organ, which confirms the identity doubt.
structures_visible: large rounded air spaces or vessels (identity uncertain)
assets.hold: organ and tissue identity unconfirmed (Commons says only "Dicot"); botanist to identify

assets.title: Normal adult blood smear
assets.source_locator: Commons file summary, original file and licensing section; inspected 2026-10-18

rights.status: file-specific licence recorded; attribution review pending
rights.creator: Keith Chambers / Scooter Project

suitability_concerns: Verify that the exact field contains the white-cell types each question requires; do not assume lymphocyte and phagocyte both visible.
Inspected 2026-10-18: no lymphocyte visible. A lymphocyte-versus-phagocyte question needs a second field.

scale.note: no scale bar; red cell diameter (~7–8 µm) is a known internal reference but is not a calibrated scale

structures_visible: three white cells; two with lobed nuclei (phagocytes / neutrophils); one larger cell with a lobed nucleus (phagocyte, type to confirm)

assets.title: Red onion plasmolysis micrograph
assets.source_locator: Commons file summary, original file and licensing section; inspected 2026-10-18

rights.status: file-specific licence recorded; attribution review pending
rights.creator: Trương Minh Khải

suitability_concerns: Caption conflicts on 400× versus 4000×; do not claim magnification or use for a size calculation without resolving it. Confirm visible plasmolysis before labelling.

Inspected 2026-10-18: PLASMOLYSIS NOT CLEARLY VISIBLE in this field, despite the title. Many cells are colourless rather than shrunken. Do not use it as the plasmolysis stimulus until a botanist confirms what it shows. It is usable as an unfamiliar example of plant epidermal cells (wall, vacuole, stoma).
structures_missing: clear plasmolysis: most protoplasts fill their cells; at most slight retraction from end walls in a few cells
assets.hold: plasmolysis not clearly visible; confirm what the field shows before mapping it to osmosis objectives

rights.creator: Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library

suitability_concerns: Real section; teacher must check epidermis, cortex and vascular bundle visibility and restrict labels to syllabus content. Caption magnification alone is not a calibrated scale bar.
